bands_removed: atmospheric water 1340-1480 and 1790-1980 nm, SWIR edge >2460 nm, blue edge <420 nm — EMIT's good_wavelengths flag retains these and reflectance there is noise, not surface signal
method: band depths against a local two-point continuum (Clark & Roush 1984); k-means on depths standardised to the scene mean; classes interpreted by DEVIATION from the scene mean, because absolute carbonate depth dominates everywhere in a carbonate-sabkha setting

headline.statement: Class 2 covers 13.9% of the imaged scene at mean albedo 0.270 — the second-darkest of the 5 classes — and is enriched +1.16 sigma in the 1730 nm C-H (bitumen) feature and +1.36 sigma in 2200 nm Al-OH (cement), with the widest albedo spread of any class (sd 0.082 against 0.026-0.044 elsewhere), consistent with mixed built materials rather than uniform sand. Broadband albedo identifies these surfaces as dark; only the narrow bands identify them as bituminous and cement-bearing, which is what determines whether a roof can be coated or must be replaced.

caveats: Spectral inference only. No field verification: classes are 'consistent with' a material, never confirmed as one.
EMIT is 60 m, one pixel 3,600 m2. Reliable only for roofs spanning a clean pixel; the top-100 ranked roofs average 1.07 ha (~3 px), smaller roofs are spectrally mixed.
This granule covers the NORTHERN part of the AOI only (granule south edge 24.353 N vs AOI south 24.29 N) with 43.5% GLT fill — roughly 46 km2 of the 195 km2 AOI.

Both the 2200 nm Al-OH and the 1730 nm C-H depth maps show faint diagonal detector striping, and mean Al-OH depth is slightly negative scene-wide, so part of that signal is instrumental rather than surface. The class-mean z-scores average over thousands of pixels and are robust to it; a per-pixel material call on a single roof is not, and should not be made from this product alone.
Carbonate absorption dominates the scene absolutely (mean depth 0.106); the classification therefore keys on deviations from that background, not on it.

corrections_applied: Class 2 was initially described as 'the darkest' class; it is the second-darkest (albedo 0.270 against class 3 at 0.250). Corrected here and computed from the data in notebooks/04_emit_hyperspectral.ipynb so it cannot drift again.
The 1730 nm C-H depth map was initially reported as free of detector striping. It shows faint striping, as the 2200 nm map does. Corrected in the caveats above.
